tagline.text: The Philippines' signature theme park, welcomed by the wizard Eldar

location.label: Location
location.text: Santa Rosa City, Laguna (near the SLEX Santa Rosa exit)

children.text: The Philippines' first full-scale theme park, opened in

, with about 30 rides including the loop coaster Space Shuttle, the Ferris wheel Wheel of Fate, and the flying theater Aguila, which soars over the Philippine skies. Just over an hour from Manila, it's an easy pick for a family outing.
Enchanted Kingdom (often shortened to EK) is the Philippines' signature theme park, located in Santa Rosa, Laguna province. Opened on
October 19, 1995

, it was the country's first theme park built to international standards, with roller coasters, water rides, children's rides, performance venues, and a dining strip spread across about 25 hectares. For most Filipinos, it's a place of childhood memories, from a school field trip or a family outing at some point growing up.

The park is divided into nine themed zones: Victoria Park, Portobello, Boulderville, Midway Boardwalk, Brooklyn Place, Spaceport, Jungle Outpost, and Eldar's Village. The park's mascot is the friendly wizard Eldar, and the mood shifts dramatically zone by zone — from the European-style street at the entrance to a prehistoric village, a jungle, and a space base — making it fun just to walk through.
The signature rides are the Space Shuttle, a roller coaster that swings forward and back through a 360-degree loop; the Wheel of Fate, a Ferris wheel about

tall; the Extreme Tower, which drops from about 120 feet; Jungle Log Jam, a log-flume ride down a steep drop; and Rio Grande Rapids, a whitewater rafting ride. The flying theater Aguila, which gives the sensation of soaring over Philippine landmarks in front of a large screen, is also popular, and new rides continue to be added.

It's more modest in scale and thrill level than the big theme parks of Korea or Japan, but on weekdays with short lines, you can ride the popular attractions several times, and admission is easy on the budget too. It suits expat families with grade-school kids, young travelers who want a fun day out with Filipino friends, and couples who want to cap off the evening with the weekend fireworks show.
The park's long-beloved icon. A shuttle-style roller coaster that accelerates instantly, flips through a loop, and comes back in reverse — short but intense.
Views take in the whole park and the Santa Rosa cityscape, and on a clear day, even Mount Makiling and Laguna de Bay in the distance. It's more romantic still at sunset or lit up at night.
An immersive film ride that soars, eagle's-eye, over the country's islands, mountains, and seas. Family members who can't handle thrill rides can enjoy this one together.

blocks.title: Jungle Log Jam and Rio Grande Rapids

children.text: The most popular water rides on a hot afternoon. You could get soaked, so bring a change of clothes or a rain poncho.
A gyro drop that climbs slowly to about 120 feet, then plunges in an instant. A must for thrill-ride fans.
A children's zone styled as a prehistoric village, with a mini train, dinosaur rides, and a small drop tower. It's full of rides even smaller children can enjoy.
On weekends and holidays, fireworks light up the sky about an hour before closing. It's the classic way to end the day, with the illuminated Ferris wheel as a backdrop.
Street performances and shows featuring Eldar and other characters take place throughout the day. Halloween and Christmas seasons bring special decorations and events.

During the regular season, hours are usually
11 AM–8 PM
, and the park is often closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Operating days and hours change by season, so check the park hours on the official website.
From Manila, take SLEX for about
40km
, exit at Santa Rosa, then head a short way along the Santa Rosa–Tagaytay road to reach the park entrance. With light traffic it takes about
an hour
, but much longer on weekend and holiday afternoons. The park has paid parking, and you must settle the fee at a designated counter before you leave. A Grab from Makati runs about
one way.
Take a bus bound for Santa Rosa, Balibago, or Calamba that passes through SLEX from Pasay Buendia, PITX, Cubao, and similar terminals, and get off near the Santa Rosa exit (Balibago). It takes about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
, for around
one way.
From the drop-off point to the park entrance is about
10 minutes
by jeepney or tricycle, for a fare of about
. At closing time, it can be hard to find transport with the crowds heading home, so allow extra time.

The park offers packages that include transport or meals, as well as educational tours for school groups. If several families are going together, chartering a 12-seater van is the most convenient, at about
for the day from Manila.
Since most rides are outdoors, the dry season,
November–May
, with little rain, is best.
December–February
has cool evening air, good for playing into the night, while
April–May
brings very strong midday sun that makes the water rides popular, though standing in line can be tiring. Bring a hat, a parasol, and a handheld fan during this period.
During the
June–October

rainy season, frequent afternoon showers and thunderstorms often force roller coasters and tall rides to pause temporarily for safety. The whole park can even close if there's a typhoon warning. On a day with rain in the forecast, the trick is to ride the popular attractions first thing in the morning.

The busiest times are weekends, holidays, summer break (April–May), and the Christmas season. Visiting on a weekday, especially Wednesday or Thursday, means shorter lines and cheaper admission than on weekends. Around year-end, the park often extends its hours and holds special events, so check the official announcements.

Most people visit from Manila as a day trip, but if you want to catch the fireworks and take it slow, staying in Santa Rosa is an option. There are business hotels around the park and near the SLEX exit, and Nuvali, an eco-friendly planned town about
10–15 minutes
away by car, has a cluster of hotels and restaurants, at about
per night. If you'd rather stay somewhere cooler, a place in Tagaytay, about
1 hour
away by car, is also a good choice.

The park has never allowed outside food or drinks, even from opening day. Instead, restaurants and stalls in every zone sell Filipino-style packed meals, fast food, pizza, snacks, and drinks. Prices run a bit higher than outside, so eating a solid meal nearby before entering is also a good tactic. After leaving the park, a popular move is dinner at the lakeside restaurants in Nuvali or a restaurant in Santa Rosa town, or heading up to Tagaytay for bulalo and buko pie.
Weekday rates are much cheaper than weekend rates. Check the official website first for online advance-purchase discounts or on-site promotions.
It's most efficient to ride popular attractions like Space Shuttle and Extreme Tower right after opening, and save the water rides for the hottest part of the day.
Admission price and which rides a child can ride depend on their height. Height is measured at the ticket booth, so have them wear sneakers.
It helps to bring a change of clothes, a plastic bag, and a towel for the water rides. Rain ponchos are also sold inside the park.
If lines are long on weekends, consider the Express Pass — it can cut wait times on major rides significantly.
Food, alcohol, cigarettes and lighters, pets, and wheeled items like scooters aren't allowed inside. Bags are checked at the entrance.
The parking lot and exits get crowded all at once right after the fireworks end. It's best to either leave right as they finish or wait a while before heading out.
Senior and disability discounts require showing ID to apply. Discounts for foreign visitors may be limited, so ask at the ticket booth.
Operating days change a lot from season to season. As of
the park normally opens Wednesday to Sunday,
11 AM–8 PM
, but during the rainy
August–September
it opened only Friday to Sunday or Thursday to Sunday, and sometimes closed temporarily in bad weather. Conversely, from
mid-December to year-end
it opens daily and extends hours to
10 PM
around Christmas. Check the
official park hours
before you go.
The park is closed Mondays and Tuesdays, and operating hours change often by season. Be sure to check the park hours and latest notices on the official website before you go.
Rain, lightning, or maintenance can stop some rides without notice, and admission is generally not refunded in that case.
Thrill rides have height and health restrictions. Don't ride them if you have a heart condition, a back or neck condition, or are pregnant.
It's easy to lose track of a child in weekend crowds. Attach a guardian's contact info to your child's clothing and agree on a meeting spot in advance.
There's a risk of heat stroke while waiting in line at midday. Drink water often and rest in the shade.
